title: The Funding: Are crypto vaults funds and curators fund managers?
headline_summary: SEC signals crypto vaults may need fund registration
blurb: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce indicates some crypto vaults may qualify as investment funds under the Securities Act, potentially requiring registration and classifying vault curators as regulated fund managers. This determination would extend direct SEC oversight to crypto investment platforms. The classification could reshape how platforms operate, govern themselves, manage compliance, market to institutional LPs, and structure capital flows.

title: India eases foreign investment rules for e-commerce companies, a win for Amazon, which lobbied to buy goods directly from Indian sellers and sell them overseas (Aditya Kalra/Reuters)
headline_summary: India eases foreign investment rules for e-commerce companies
blurb: India eased foreign investment restrictions for e-commerce companies, allowing direct purchases from Indian sellers destined for export markets. Amazon successfully lobbied for the regulatory change and can now source inventory directly from local suppliers for international resale. The policy shift opens sourcing opportunities for cross-border e-commerce operators and signals India's determination to attract foreign retail investment through liberalized FDI policies.

title: BIS warns USD stablecoins can evade capital controls
headline_summary: BIS warns USD stablecoins enable capital control evasion
blurb: BIS warned that USD stablecoins enable capital control evasion, creating serious regulatory pressure globally. The Bank for International Settlements flagged stablecoins' capacity to circumvent cross-border financial oversight and capital flow restrictions effectively. This matters to VC portfolios: tightening stablecoin regulation will constrain adoption for fintech and crypto companies building on stablecoin infrastructure, reshaping their access to dollar liquidity.

title: EDX Markets Closes $76M Series C Led by SBI Holdings
headline_summary: EDX Markets closes $76M Series C led by SBI Holdings
blurb: EDX Markets, an institutional-only crypto trading venue with its own central clearinghouse, closed a $76 million Series C funding round. SBI Holdings, the Tokyo-listed financial group, led the round and became a strategic investor. The funding signals strong institutional appetite for regulated crypto infrastructure and reflects growing mainstream finance acceptance of professional-grade digital asset trading as a core business capability.

title: Spain-based Multiverse Computing, which shrinks LLMs to reduce energy and compute costs, raised a $570M Series C at a $1.7B valuation (Amelia Isaacs/Pathfounders)
headline_summary: Multiverse Computing raises $570M Series C for LLM compression
blurb: Spain-based Multiverse Computing raised $570M in Series C funding at a $1.7B post-money valuation. Its quantum-inspired compression tech shrinks large language models by up to 95%, cutting energy use and compute costs. For infrastructure-focused VCs, this validates the market thesis that LLM efficiency and cost reduction are first-class investment priorities.

title: European startup with SpaceX ambitions seeks $300M at $2B valuation
headline_summary: European space startup seeks $300M at $2B valuation
blurb: European space startup seeks $300M in funding at a $2B valuation. Founded by Hélène Huby, who joined Airbus in 2013 with no background in satellites or rocket technology, the company is positioning itself to challenge SpaceX in commercial space launch. This funding signals European venture appetite for deep-tech infrastructure plays and reflects confidence in emerging challengers to US space dominance.

title: Spain’s Multiverse Computing hits unicorn status after raising €500 million Series C at €1.5 billion valuation
headline_summary: Multiverse Computing raises €500M Series C at €1.5B unicorn valuation
blurb: Multiverse Computing raised €500 million at €1.5 billion valuation in Series C, achieving unicorn status as a European AI company. Forgepoint Capital International, BNPP SIVF, and Bullhound Capital led the round, marking a 5x jump from the previous Series B valuation. Late-stage capital flowing into sovereign AI startups signals European VCs see structural competitive advantages in building independent infrastructure.

title: The Exploration Company in talks to raise $300M at a $2B valuation
headline_summary: Exploration Company raises $300M at $2B valuation for reusable spacecraft
blurb: The Exploration Company is raising $300M for Europe's first reusable space capsule. The Munich-based startup, founded six years ago, targets a $2B valuation in this round. The company aims to reduce European reliance on non-European launch providers and build sovereign space infrastructure. Deep-tech space companies addressing geopolitical autonomy have become core category bets for European venture investors seeking supply-chain independence and defensible, long-term infrastructure plays.

title: Multiverse Raising Funds at $1.7 Billion Value to Cut AI Costs
headline_summary: Multiverse Computing raises $570M at $1.7B valuation for AI cost reduction
blurb: Multiverse Computing closed a $570 million funding round, reaching a $1.7 billion valuation with investor backing for AI cost-reduction tools. The Spanish software company helps enterprises significantly reduce spending when building and deploying artificial intelligence systems at scale. Capital flowing to efficiency plays signals venture's conviction that as corporate AI budgets balloon, tools cutting infrastructure costs will command premium valuations.

title: 1st Serbian unicorn! Ominimo Hits $1.6B Valuation after EBRD supported Series B
headline_summary: Serbian Ominimo becomes first local unicorn at $1.6B valuation
blurb: Ominimo, a Serbian startup, has reached unicorn status with a $1.6 billion valuation. The Series B round included participation from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's investment arm, marking Ominimo as the first Serbian company to achieve the milestone. The funding signals institutional capital flowing into Eastern European tech and validates growing investor appetite for startups across the region.

title: Quantum computing startup Multiverse bags $570M at $2.3B valuation: The story behind its 96x growth in 4 years
headline_summary: Multiverse Computing closes $570M Series C at $2.3B valuation
blurb: Multiverse Computing raised $570 million in Series C funding at a $2.3 billion post-money valuation, marking 96x growth in just four years. The quantum computing startup's momentum reflects rising enterprise demand for quantum applications beyond pure research. For VC investors watching deeptech, this signals that quantum computing has moved from speculative moonshot into practical, fundable category with real customer traction.

title: How US companies flipped from "tokenmaxxing" to "thrift-maxxing", mixing cheaper Chinese models with OpenAI and Anthropic, threatening the labs' IPO valuations (Wall Street Journal)
headline_summary: US companies mix cheap Chinese AI models with OpenAI, threatening valuations
blurb: US companies are mixing cheaper Chinese AI models with OpenAI and Anthropic offerings in production stacks. The shift from 'tokenmaxxing' to 'thrift-maxxing' reflects cost discipline spreading across enterprises and startups rapidly. This spending diversification directly threatens lab IPO valuations, proving that premium AI vendors lack sustainable pricing power, durable moats, or meaningful vendor lock-in against increasingly cost-conscious buyers worldwide.

title: Big Companies Are Starting to Hire Again, Defying Predictions of AI Wipeout
headline_summary: Big companies resume hiring as AI adoption drives labor augmentation
blurb: After a hiring freeze, major companies in tech, transportation, and defense are resuming recruitment at scale. Firms report needing more staff to work alongside AI systems, not replace them. This matters for VCs: labor augmentation reshapes talent scarcity, determines where hiring bottlenecks emerge, and reveals which skill gaps will define competitive edges for startups building AI-dependent products and services.

title: Dealroom: defense giants such as Lockheed Martin have participated in a record $4.1B worth of VC rounds YTD, as drones and autonomous systems transform warfare (Financial Times)
headline_summary: Defense giants deploy record $4.1B in autonomous warfare VC
blurb: Defense giants deployed a record $4.1B into VC rounds focused on drones and autonomous systems in 2026. Lockheed Martin and traditional contractors are now operating as venture capitalists, backing startups that reshape modern warfare. For the VC ecosystem, the shift signals that institutional defense capital sees autonomous systems as the next frontier—and that legacy players will invest early rather than risk missing transformative technologies.

title: Europe's high regulatory bar could spark new crypto industry M&A wave
headline_summary: Europe's stricter crypto rules spark predicted consolidation wave
blurb: Europe's tightening regulatory framework is reshaping crypto's M&A landscape: smaller startups without in-house compliance become acquisition targets while established players with expertise and capital acquire them at lower valuations, systematically dominating the market. Consolidation accelerates as larger firms eliminate weaker competitors. For VCs, this signals a critical inflection—the fragmented startup era ends and future winners are regulatory-compliant infrastructure platforms.

title: Elon Musk’s Boring Company reportedly raising funding at a $20 billion valuation
headline_summary: Boring Company raises funding at $20B valuation
blurb: Boring Company is raising new funding at a $20 billion valuation in active negotiations. Elon Musk's tunneling infrastructure startup is pursuing the major capital round to accelerate tunnel construction and expand operational capacity. The valuation signals sustained venture capital appetite for hardware-intensive deeptech infrastructure plays and reflects strong ongoing investor confidence in Musk-led companies despite the company's current limited commercial revenue base.

title: Bitcoin ETF weekly trading volume falls to lowest since October 2024 as ether funds lead inflows again
headline_summary: Bitcoin ETF volume slumps to Oct 2024 low as Ether attracts capital
blurb: Bitcoin ETF weekly trading volumes have fallen to their lowest level since October 2024. Ether funds, despite holding roughly one-eighth as much capital under management, have attracted nearly equal inflows over the past three weeks. This rotation signals shifting investor sentiment and capital allocation pressure within crypto markets, with liquidity moving toward Ethereum and alternative assets.

title: OpenAI Raised Its Infrastructure Plans to $750 Billion
headline_summary: OpenAI escalates $750 billion infrastructure spending plan
blurb: OpenAI disclosed a $750 billion infrastructure investment plan to secure compute capacity for frontier AI development and deployment. The company will construct and operate training and hosting facilities over multiple years. For venture investors, this demonstrates the unprecedented capital concentration required in AI infrastructure—a dynamic reshaping startup funding intensity, valuations, and competitive positioning across the entire sector.

title: AMD and Anthropic Sign Major Chips-and-Investment Deal
headline_summary: AMD and Anthropic ink major chips-and-investment strategic partnership
blurb: AMD and Anthropic have signed a major strategic partnership combining semiconductor chips and investment capital. The deal pairs AMD's advanced chip technology with Anthropic's AI capabilities through preferred hardware supply and substantial direct equity investment. For VCs tracking AI infrastructure capital, this signals semiconductor manufacturers are now co-investing in leading AI companies—reshaping how AI companies access both cutting-edge hardware and venture funding.

title: Payments M&A spools up
headline_summary: Payments M&A accelerating across fintech sector
blurb: Payments M&A is spooling up across North America and Europe. Fintech acquirers, banks, and strategic buyers are increasing dealmaking in payment processors, embedded finance platforms, and infrastructure systems—a clear signal of sector maturation. This uptick in M&A velocity creates exit windows for venture-backed fintechs and forces LPs and partners to adjust return expectations and valuations as the sector pivots from hypergrowth toward consolidation and profitability.

title: Databricks is Raising a Strategic Round of Funding at a $188 Billion Valuation
headline_summary: Databricks reaches $188 billion valuation in strategic round
blurb: Databricks secured strategic funding at a $188 billion valuation, entering the ultra-exclusive tier of venture's most valuable private companies worldwide. Major investors continue deploying substantial capital into AI-native data infrastructure as enterprises accelerate AI workload operationalization and scale. The valuation confirms sustained conviction that unified data-to-AI platforms justify premium market multiples and represent a defining long-term investment theme.

title: Citadel Securities invests $400M in Crypto.com at $20B valuation
headline_summary: Citadel invests $400M in Crypto.com at $20B valuation
blurb: Citadel Securities is investing $400M in Crypto.com, valuing the exchange at $20B. The market maker's nine-figure commitment signals institutional demand for crypto infrastructure and represents one of the largest capital infusions into an exchange. For VCs tracking valuations, this sets a floor: it shows where major finance firms price leading crypto platforms and suggests the sector's shift to institutional adoption has durably changed.

title: UK pension providers in talks for £1bn fund
headline_summary: UK pension funds launch £1bn+ scale-up investment fund
blurb: UK pension providers Nest, Railpen, and Border to Coast are launching the UK Scale-Up Fund targeting innovative private companies. Backed by the British Business Bank, the fund targets more than £1bn in capital commitments for UK-based scale-ups at growth stage. This move signals major institutional LP conviction in the UK innovation market and introduces new competition in the later-stage funding landscape.

title: Manchester startup Nuclear Turbines snaps £15M led by IQ Capital to make nuclear power as cheap as jet fuel
headline_summary: Nuclear Turbines raises £15M to slash nuclear power costs
blurb: Nuclear Turbines raised £15M in a funding round led by IQ Capital. The Manchester startup, founded by Jeremy Owston (ex-BAE Systems nuclear engineer), is developing turbine technology to make nuclear power cost-competitive with fossil fuels. Cheaper nuclear unlocks a major capital allocation opportunity in climate tech as energy costs remain a gating factor for grid decarbonization.

title: Shein reveals slowing profits and a quarterly loss ahead of Hong Kong IPO
headline_summary: Shein files Hong Kong IPO amid 38.7% profit decline
blurb: Shein filed its Hong Kong IPO prospectus, disclosing $41.8 billion in 2025 revenue and $2.064 billion in net profit. While sales grew 8% year-over-year, profit fell 38.7%, indicating significant margin compression at massive scale. The filing tests a critical thesis: whether ultra-high-growth, low-margin consumer platforms can sustain profitability and positive unit economics under the scrutiny and governance demands of public markets.

title: China Chipmaker CXMT Jumps 466% in Debut After Blockbuster IPO
headline_summary: China's AI Chipmaker CXMT Soars 466% on Shanghai IPO Debut
blurb: CXMT Corp. surged 466% on its Shanghai trading debut, becoming China's largest onshore-listed company. The AI chipmaker's blockbuster performance reflects intense investor appetite for domestic semiconductor leaders building critical AI infrastructure. For venture investors, the IPO establishes a major valuation benchmark for chip manufacturers and signals strong confidence in Chinese startups, underscoring intensifying geopolitical competition for semiconductor and AI infrastructure dominance.
